entities.summary:
Landry of Paris: A Saint of Healing and Charity

Born in the 6th century CE, Landry of Paris was a Bishop of Paris who dedicated his life to the service of others. He is canonized as a saint by both the Roman Catholic Church and the Orthodox Church, and his feast day is celebrated on June 10.

Landry's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he established a hospital dedicated to St. Christopher, which later became the Hôtel-Dieu de Paris. This institution, which still operates today, has provided medical care to countless individuals throughout French history.

Landry's commitment to healing and charity has had a lasting impact on the city of Paris and the world at large. His selfless dedication to the service of others serves as a powerful reminder of the importance of compassion and kindness.

"The greatest glory in living lies not in never falling, but in rising every time we fall," Landry's own words on the importance of perseverance in the face of adversity. His legacy continues to inspire generations to come.
